word_linkages.word: sięgać po cudze (imperfective) sięgnąć po cudze

glosses: odebrać coś bezprawnie, posługując się przemocą

examples.text: Uzbrojeni w pistolety napastnicy sterroryzowali całą obsługę i zrabowali precjoza, warte być może nawet ponad 100 tys. zł.

glosses: zabrać wiele rzeczy z budynku, pokoju lub innego terenu bezprawnie i posługując się przemocą

examples.text: Tułaczka większości wysiedlonych trwała do końca wojny, a ci, którzy wrócili do rodzinnych wsi, znajdowali gospodarstwa doszczętnie zrabowane albo tylko zgliszcza.

glosses: To pillage, take or destroy all the goods of, by force (as in war); to raid, sack.

examples.text: The mercenaries plundered the small town.
The shopkeeper was plundered of his possessions by the burglar.

Now Azaēlos, the king of Syria, made war on the Israelites and their king Jehu, and ravaged the eastern parts of the country across the Jordan […] spreading fire everywhere and plundering everything and inflicting violence on all who fell into his hands.
The mercenaries plundered all the goods they found.

glosses: To take by force or wrongfully; to commit robbery or looting, to raid.

examples.text: “Now to plunder, mateys!” screamed a buccaneer, to cries of “Arrgh!” and “Aye!” all around.

glosses: To make extensive (over)use of, as if by plundering; to use or use up wrongfully.

examples.text: The miners plundered the jungle for its diamonds till it became a muddy waste.
The Serb teed up Steve Davis, who crossed low for Graziano Pellè to plunder his fifth league goal of the campaign.
The Hessian kept his choicest plunder in a sack that never left his person, for fear that his comrades would steal it.
[…] till a long-legged boy brought him out of his revery, by an offer to carry his “plunder,” in whatsoever direction he might desire to direct his steps.

glosses: The crime of amassing ill-gotten wealth by public officials through a combination or series of overt criminal acts.
